scenario.title: Battle of Konitsa
intro.text:
BATTLE OF KONITSA - 25 DEC 1947

Konitsa, Epirus

Our struggle for a free Greece is now entering a decisive phase. Our political leadership has decided that we need a major city as capital for our government to gain further international validity for our fight. The choice has fallen on the city Konitsa at the Albanian border and the battle is already under way. But reinforcements are on the way to Konitsa to relieve the garrison. Fend off the attacks of the Athenian mercenary troops and bring the liberation of Konitsa to a successful end!

GOAL Capture all VH!
header.act: ACT IV — THE WAR IN THE MOUNTAINS
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-24-0-briliant.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.reaction-24-0-briliant.text: The December assault broke the government positions before the British bridgehead was ready. Britain reversed the result and the foreign ministries ignored it. We have spent three years arguing over which fact mattered more.
line.reaction-24-1-victory-tactical.text: ELAS took most of its Athens objectives while British formations continued to arrive. The cadres who came out remember winning streets and losing the city. They distrust anyone who offers a simple lesson.
line.reaction-24-2-lose.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.reaction-24-2-lose.text: I carried the ceasefire instructions through districts we no longer held. Varkiza ended the battle and left unarmed people waiting to learn whether the state would distinguish peace from surrender. Many did not wait long.
line.callback-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.callback-0.text: The December assault proved ELAS could contest the capital. It also proved that taking an airfield could not isolate Athens from British power outside Greece. We inherit both lessons.
line.callback-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.callback-1.text: The district defence brought more cadres out of Athens. It also gave Britain time to make the withdrawal unavoidable. You saved men whose next orders now come from the mountains.
line.scene-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-0.text: Two men reached us from Thessaly. One boycotted the March election; the other voted. The same gendarmerie truck took both. Only one escaped before the ship sailed for the islands.
line.scene-1.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.scene-1.text: A seat in that parliament would have made the terror legal, not made the Left safe.
line.scene-2.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.scene-2.text: An empty seat spoke too. It told every organiser in Athens that the mountains were now our only argument.
line.scene-3.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.scene-3.text: The greater mistake was waiting while the factories, unions, and army still held our people. We cannot recover 1946. A government in Konitsa would at least give this struggle offices, a population, and Greek soil.
line.scene-4.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.scene-4.text: A missed uprising is not repaired by ordering a mountain army to behave like a city. Konitsa gives the National Army walls, relief roads, and coordinates for every gun it owns.
line.scene-5.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.scene-5.text: The inhabitants are digging beside the garrison. If we call Konitsa a capital before we enter it, we have already stopped asking what they want.
line.decision.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.decision.text: Do we commit the main force to the town, or cut its roads and keep a reserve free for the relief columns?
line.decision.choice.storm-the-city.text: Commit the main force to taking Konitsa as a provisional capital.
line.decision.choice.storm-the-city.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give infantry and artillery 20 experience, and restore the core to at least nine strength with full ammunition.
line.decision.choice.isolate-the-garriso: Cut the roads, contain the garrison, and preserve a mobile reserve.
Give reconnaissance 20 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.choice-a-0.text: Then publish rules for the town before the assault: no requisition without receipt, no arrest by local score-settling, and a marked hospital.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-a-1.text: Publish them. Konitsa is taken to govern, not to raid. The reserve follows the assault once the road is open.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikos Zachariadis
line.choice-b-0.text: A siege without possession will not make the Democratic Government more real. Do not return with captured lorries and call mobility a political result.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Markos Vafiadis
line.choice-b-1.text: I will return with an army. Cut the roads, hit relief columns, and leave the garrison the fixed battle it prepared for itself.
